poems:
Six o'clock.
The radio man says the beltway is already unhappy.
He says it the same way every day,
like a man reading his own name off a headstone.
Two alarms in the same house, set one minute apart, neither of them for the same person.

6:02. The leash makes its one sound
and the whole dog reorganizes.
Sneakers by the door, laces still tied.

Preheat.
Grease the pan.
Do not open the door for twenty minutes.
Do not open it.
Do not.
The route begins at a corner with no bench, no shelter, and one woman already standing on it.
Somewhere it is already light and somewhere it isn't, and both places want the same thing from you, which is up.
An electric toothbrush running in an empty bathroom, the owner three rooms away, looking for a shoe.

Snooze, v.
To agree to a thing you have no intention of honoring.

6:09. The stairs get louder
as the household descends by weight class.
At 6:10 the bus is three streets out and the shoe is under the couch and everyone in the house knows both facts.

First cigarette on the loading dock.
He has been up two hours.
This is the part he does alone.
Through the wall: I said I'd handle it, so I'll handle it.
Milk crates stacked outside a bodega, a man cutting the plastic band with his house key.
At 6:14 the second parent has still not moved. This is a negotiation with no words in it and a clear winner.
Buses lean at the curb, hissing, patient as horses.

DRIP LG      2.45
SUB          2.45
TIP  _______
THANK YOU HAVE A GREAT DAY
A crossing guard's vest on a kitchen chair.

You will pack the lunch.
You will forget the note you meant to put in it.
Both are already true.
The traffic voice pronounces the interstate numbers with real affection, the way a man names racehorses.

6:20. Orange juice in a small glass,
the vitamins lined up like chess pieces.
Hair wet. Coat on. Keys.
At 6:22 the water heater in a four-person house begins its slow public failure.
Ice on the inside of the truck windshield, or no ice, depending. Either way he is scraping something.
Blue recycling bin on its side.

Take with food.
Do not lie down for thirty minutes.
Do not lie down.
Six twenty-six. Whatever you rehearsed at eleven last night is gone. What survived the night is the part you actually meant.
On the fourth floor a man irons one shirt sleeve for longer than a shirt sleeve requires.
Cereal, then the phone. Now it is soup.
The 6:29 is a different train from the 6:34 in ways only its riders could defend.

Half past.
Every shower in the building is running
and the top floor has opinions about the pressure.

6:31. Day shift arrives smelling of outside.
Night shift has forgotten outside exists.

The dog gets fed.
The dog is the only one here whose morning is going as planned.

Frost or dew or nothing.
The grass has been doing something all night and nobody looked.
Backpack by the door with one strap chewed.
At 6:35 somebody's mother in another time zone is eating lunch and thinking about calling.
Baked at four. Toast by six.
Four cars at the pharmacy drive-through before the pharmacy opens. Nobody's engine off.

Morning, n.
The period during which everything you own is somewhere else.
Two hands on a steering wheel, a parked car, a driveway, the engine running and nothing moving yet.
Six forty. If it is Saturday none of this applies and the house is a different animal entirely.
Through the floor: Did you take the thing. Take the thing.

6:42. The school boiler wakes its radiators
one clank at a time.
Steam off a manhole. Nobody looks up.
The third-favorite podcast, because the first two have not posted yet.
Whoever is going to be late is already late and has not accepted it.
A woman on the platform eats a banana with the efficiency of somebody who has decided this counts.

Keys, wallet, badge.
The pat-down of a man who trusts nobody, himself included.

6:48. The garage fridge surrenders a squeezable yogurt
to a small emissary.
A church parking lot, three cars in it.

6:50. The weather is consulted twice
and believed neither time.
The shoe is found. No investigation follows.
In the elevator of a building where nothing has started yet, a man practices saying a name out loud.

6:53. The bus stop's first two commuters
stand a polite country apart.
At 6:54 an alarm goes off in an empty room and does its entire job for nobody.

6:55. The dishes look at everyone leaving,
and lose.

6:56. The car keys are not where keys live.
A house-wide referendum begins.

6:57. Someone runs back in for the thing.
The thing is in their hand the whole time.
Somewhere a bell rings at seven and somewhere at eight, and the difference between those two houses is enormous, and nobody in either has time to consider it.

The house has emptied or it hasn't.
The furnace keeps going either way, being paid to.
